haiku-low.q1: They sign in normally. The account is matched by sub, not email, so start_session runs. The stored email is not changed.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's password on the confirm page. Then the Google link is inserted, failed_logins reset, and start_session runs.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account locks 15 minutes, failed_logins resets to 0, and the pending link is deleted.
haiku-low.q4: Unlinked, verified, no matching user: create a passwordless verified user, insert the identity, start a session. Unverified: refused, nothing created, use email and password.
haiku-low.q5: Error page, nothing changes. The state entry expired after 10 minutes, or was already deleted by the first callback, so the second load fails.
haiku-low.q6: A new 14-day sessions row and sid cookie. If a sid cookie already existed, its sessions row is deleted first, even if it belonged to another user.
haiku-low.q7: No password or email match is required, only that sid belongs to the saved user. If the Google account is linked to another user, it is refused: already in use.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis under oauth_state:<state>, for 10 minutes. The callback reads and deletes it in one step, or Redis expiry removes it. Verifier and ID token are dropped after use.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis as pending_link:<id>, holding user ID, sub and next. The browser holds the random ID in an HttpOnly cookie. Success, lockout, refusal or 10-minute expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the Postgres user_identities table, permanent. Primary key google_sub gives one user per Google account. UNIQUE user_id gives one Google account per user.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees an error page and nothing changes. They must start Google sign-in again. There is no retry.
haiku-low.q12: The saved mode (login or link) in the Redis state entry tells the callback which applies. For link, the sid must belong to the user ID saved at start, else an error.

sonnet.q1: Accounts are matched by sub, not email, so the changed email does not matter. The sub is found in user_identities, start_session is called, and the user is redirected to next or /home. The lockout fields are not checked.
sonnet.q2: The user must enter the existing account's password on the confirm page (only if that user has a password; if not, they are refused and told to use the reset email). The pending link is saved in Redis and a cookie is set, with no session yet. The account must not be locked, and it must not already have another Google link. On the right password the identity row is inserted and start_session is called.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account is locked for 15 minutes and failed_logins resets to 0. The pending link is deleted and the login page shows 'Account temporarily locked'. Before 5, the confirm page is shown again for retries until the 10 minutes end. No identity row is inserted.
sonnet.q4: If the email is verified and no user has it (compared lowercased), a user is created with no password and a verified email. A user_identities row is inserted and start_session is called. If Google says the email is not verified, the sign-in is refused. The user is pointed to email and password, and nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Both cases give an error page and change nothing. After 12 minutes the state has expired (10-minute limit). A second load finds the state already used, because it is read and deleted in one step.
sonnet.q6: It creates the same session as password login. start_session first deletes the sessions row for any sid the browser sent, even if it belongs to a different user. It then inserts a new sessions row lasting 14 days, slid forward on each request, and sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). No other kind of session is created.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email comparison are required, and no session is created. The sid must belong to the user ID saved at start, or it is an error page. If the sub is linked to another user, it is refused with 'Google account already in use'. If it is already linked to this user, the user is told it is already linked. If this user already has a different Google link, it is refused.
sonnet.q8: They are kept in Redis under oauth_state:<state> for 10 minutes, along with the mode, return page, next and user ID for link mode. The callback reads and deletes the entry in one step, or Redis expires it.
sonnet.q9: It is held in Redis as pending_link:<id>, holding the user ID, the Google sub and next, for 10 minutes. The browser refers to it by a pending ID cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax) that holds the random id. The pending link is deleted on confirm success, lockout, refusal, or expiry, and the cookie is cleared when the link is deleted.
sonnet.q10: It is stored in the Postgres table user_identities (google_sub TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id BIGINT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE). The primary key on google_sub gives one user per Google account. The UNIQUE on user_id gives one Google account per user.
sonnet.q11: The user sees an error page and nothing changes. There is no retry, so the user must start again.
sonnet.q12: The start step saves the mode (login or link) in the Redis state entry, and the callback reads it from there. For link mode, the start step also saves the signed-in user ID. At the callback the browser's sid must belong to that saved user ID, otherwise it is an error page and nothing changes.
